title: Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications
author: Alec Kriebel
date_scope: Declared selected Zenodo edition publication date; created 2026-10-07. Manuscript date is not separately certified earliest public priority.
page_title: Metric rigidity for singular Kähler–Einstein Fanos and cubic compactifications | Alec Kriebel
meta_description: A sharp Cartier-index rigidity criterion for singular Kähler–Einstein Fano varieties and its application to cubic metric compactifications modulo conjugation.
abstract: We deduce a sharp Cartier-index criterion for complex-structure rigidity on singular Kähler–Einstein Fano varieties. If −K_X = rL with L ample Cartier and r > dim(X)/2 + 1, then the tangent sheaf is stable and every parallel orthogonal complex structure on the regular locus equals the given one or its negative. The proof combines the decomposition theorem of Druel–Guenancia–Păun with a Hilbert-polynomial index bound and local positive-Ricci curvature. Applied to cubic n-fold limits, n ≥ 5, it identifies the ordinary metric Gromov–Hausdorff compactification with cubic GIT modulo conjugation, including the singular boundary. We also record the complex-preserving comparison as an attributed consequence of the unrestricted ordinary-double-point gap, Li–Liu's global Reeb minimum, and Spotti–Sun's established transfer. The complex algebraic comparison is already publicly stated in stronger form by Kong–Shen–Zhao–Zhao; no first-solution claim is made.
accessible_explanation: A complex algebraic variety also has an underlying real geometric shape. Forgetting its complex structure can sometimes identify several varieties with the same metric. This note gives a high-index criterion intended to force the complex structure to be determined up to conjugation, and applies it to singular limits of cubic hypersurfaces of dimension at least five.
central_result: For a positive-dimensional irreducible normal projective complex klt Fano variety with a weak Kähler–Einstein current of bounded potentials, smooth on the regular locus, and an actual ample Cartier root −K_X=rL for a positive integer r>dim(X)/2+1, the paper deduces stable tangent sheaves on finite quasi-étale covers and uniqueness up to sign of parallel orthogonal complex structures. Assuming the cited external ordinary-double-point upper-gap theorem, the cubic application identifies ordinary metric Gromov–Hausdorff compactification with cubic GIT modulo conjugation, including singular boundary fibers.
conditionality: The general rigidity criterion uses the cited singular KE decomposition theorem. The cubic compactification application also relies on the pinned OpenAI upper-gap theorem, Li–Liu global Reeb minimization and the established Spotti–Sun transfer. The note provides no independent proof of the upper-gap theorem.
limitations: The root is an actual ample Cartier line bundle and the strict inequality r>dim(X)/2+1 is essential.
The cubic application is for dimensions n≥5 and actual polarized GH limits; arbitrary metric completions of nonsmoothable weak KE varieties are outside the assertion.
The index sharpness example is a product of projective spaces, not a cubic-fourfold counterexample.
The comparison asserted here is a homeomorphism of complex points and an ordinary metric quotient; no scheme, stack, moduli-functor, or all-nonclosed-orbit comparison is deduced.
No effective GH-distance estimate, formal verification, first-solution or first-priority claim is made.
